question_or_symptom: Dispatch completion and D2H acceptance can race a packet-retirement signal update unless the cross-extension ordering is explicit.
observation: The pinned fixture starts with signed signal value one and one same-owner unsatisfied EQ-zero wait. The generation-valid retirement listener stores zero at packet-retire tick R; the CP7 SIGNAL_COMPLETION is exactly R+1 and is emitted before DISPATCH_COMPLETION. Runtime validates both completions and their request/trace/tick identities before accepting the 64-byte XOR D2H result.
conclusion: A signal mirror is a causal boundary only when retirement, signal completion, dispatch completion, and data visibility have a checked total order.
decision: Use only the generation-checked real retirement listener to mirror CP7, enforce R then R+1 then dispatch completion ordering without overflow, retain both canonical records, and permit D2H only after the signal and dispatch results are fully validated.
invalidated_assumptions: A one-tick timer can stand in for packet retirement.
Dispatch completion may be consumed before the signal completion that proves the GPU store boundary.
